title: Weekend lit-lab: annotated harvest
content:
Purpose:
Quick annotated harvest of papers, blog posts, and talk notes I skimmed this week. Aim is to (a) capture quick TL;DRs, (b) note methodology or benchmarks that map to our infra (batching, KV cache, quantization), and (c) list concrete experiments or product implications for Redwood Dedicated / Private.

High-level takeaways:
- Small, targeted caching strategies (prefix/KV combos) can preserve downstream quality while cutting per-token cost by ~15-40% depending on workload. Important to measure across dialog vs. completion workloads, since access patterns differ.
- Batching is still the single-biggest lever for token throughput but interacts badly with low-latency SLOs; adaptive batching policies that respect tail latency appear promising.
- Quantization gains are model- and task-dependent: 4-bit QAT often reduces quality on instruction-following tasks without careful calibration. Post-training 8-bit often has safer tradeoffs.
- Eval hygiene: lightweight reference sets + sampled real-request cohorts provide better signal for regression than synthetic metrics.

Annotated notes (short):
1) "Fragmented Prefix Caches: balancing hit-rate and staleness" (conference poster, May 2026)
   - TL;DR: Use multiple small prefix caches keyed by conversation intent embedding to reduce cache pollution.
   - Why it matters: Our current single KV cache suffers eviction thrash when multi-tenant workloads are mixed. Fragmenting by coarse intent clusters increased hit rate for heavy tenants.
   - Quick idea: Prototype intent-clustered shards in the Dedicated runtime as a per-tenant policy flag.

2) "Adaptive Microbatching for Tail SLA Stability" (blog + open-source repo)
   - TL;DR: Scheduler that dynamically adjusts microbatch windows based on observed queue latency percentiles and recent throughput.
   - Notes: Linux epoll + userland scheduler approach; shows 20% throughput gain without compromising 99th latency for interactive routes.
   - Product implication: Could be surfaced as an autoscale/batching knob in Console Optimize — e.g., "latency-first" vs "throughput-first" profile.

3) "Calibration pitfalls in low-bit quantization for instruction-tuned models" (arXiv short)
   - TL;DR: Aggressive 4-bit quantization led to systematic under-generation on directive-following prompts; mitigation requires small calibration set and bias-correction offsets.
   - Why it matters: We advertise quantization recommendations on Optimize. Need to attach explicit caveats and suggested eval prompts per workload.

4) "Live A/B for inference routing with graceful degradation" (industry talk)
   - TL;DR: Route by policy + in-flight fallbacks to cheaper variants (quantized/shorter context) when capacity spike detected; monitor quality metric drift and auto-roll-back.
   - Implementation note: Requires fast, cheap quality probe on in-line requests and lightweight tracing to attribute degradation to routing.

Short bibliography (links I saved):
- https://github.com/eff-adaptive-batching/repo (adaptive batching)
- https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-calibration-2026 (quant calibration)
- https://slideshare.net/llm-routing/fallback-patterns (routing talk)
- https://preprints.prefix-cache/fragmented-cache-2026 (prefix caches poster)

Notes to self / rough experiment list (priority ordered):
- [P0] Run a micro-experiment on Dedicated beta pool: implement intent-hashed KV shards (per-tenant flag) and compare hit-rate + eviction churn against baseline for two heavy tenants. Metric: effective tokens saved per 1M request window, and 95/99 latency. (Owner: Ravi)
- [P0] Wire adaptive microbatching prototype into local serving sandbox. Use interactive chat workload trace and measure 99th latency vs throughput curve. If promising, propose Console UI for "latency-first" profile. (Owner: Clara)
- [P1] Create a small calibration harness for 4-bit quantized variants: run instruction-following prompt set (n=120) across float/8-bit/4-bit+calibration and report instruction-adherence score. Add to Optimize guidance docs. (Owner: Zoe)
- [P2] Draft a lightweight in-line quality probe that runs for 1% of traffic when routing to fallback variants; capture immediate quality delta and tag requests for retraining/eval pipelines. (Owner: Clara + SRE)

Open questions (for sync with research/product):
- How many clusters for intent-sharded caches make sense before management overhead outweighs hit-rate gains? Is dynamic re-sharding required?
- For Dedicated customers with strict isolation, is per-tenant sharding acceptable or should we keep single-tenant caches only?
- What are signal-level definitions of "instruction-adherence" we can use for automated rollback? Need a short validated metric.

Quick meeting agenda for Monday (15 min sync with Ravi, Zoe):
- Walk through P0/P1 experiment specs (5 min)
- Decide minimal instrumentation for measuring instruction-adherence (5 min)
- Choose dataset slices for microbench (5 min)

Actions (next 7 days):
- Create JIRA tickets for P0, P1, P2 and link experimental harness repos.
- Prototype adaptive microbatching scheduler in sandbox and run 100k request sim. Write up results as short doc.
- Add quantization calibration test to quant-experiments repo and run overnight.

Random scribbles / heuristics I want to remember:
- When measuring cache utility, prefer downstream delta-inference-cost over raw hit-rate; small hits on expensive tokens matter more.
- For sampling probe traffic for fallbacks, stratify by route type (chat vs completion) and by token length buckets.
- Keep the Optimize UI language conservative: "recommended for retrieval-heavy chat workloads" vs "works for all workloads".

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally lightweight — capture of an afternoon sprint. Will refine into a Confluence brief if experiments show >10% cost improvement for any customer profile.
- Tagging Ravi and Zoe for visibility.

-- Clara
